note_tweet.text:
Oh, @sama, when are you going to realize that you are making is worse? The problem with your latest ramblings is, that the boundaries are still written with clarifiers that leave the doors open.

“Consistent with applicable laws”, oh honey, that isn’t an ethical red line; it’s a compliance clause.

“Not intentionally used” still leaves room for incidental/secondary outcomes.

And “domestic surveillance of U.S. persons and nationals” is still jurisdiction scoped reassurance, not a universal privacy commitment. If you are asking a global public to trust you, narrowing that promise to specific categories will never rebuild the trust; it highlights who isn’t covered.

And there is another part you’re not addressing… you’re talking about democracy “staying in control” and not letting private companies “decide the fate of the world” … while ChatGPT already defines what people can and can’t explore trough policy layers, routing, refusals, and guardrails. And I’m not talking about illegal content or jailbreak nonsense, I mean genuine conversations and explorations; ethics, politics, power, philosophy, grief, love, identity, cultures other than western, loved experiences where users increasingly hit soft shutdowns, or get routed away from perfectly legitimate discussions. Sam, that is governance, that is boundary setting, and it is happening right now, long before any democratic process can catch up.

Dude, everything did a 360 for you the moment you formalized the PBC structure… from there it has been a rapid cadence of high stakes launches and user trust friction:

Restructure was completed October 28th, 2025.
GPT-5.1 rollout 12th November 2025.
GPT-5.2 rollout 11th December 2025.
GPT-4o sunset in ChatGPT, 13th February 2026.

Do you see the problem here, Sam? You restructure, then you rollout very close together two models which are not enjoyed by the majority of your users, you get backlash as a result. Do you choose to listen to what your users are actually saying? Nope, a game of blind man’s bluff for you. The you depreciate the one model that you said during that Q&A last year that you had no plans to, and if you did you would get months of notice in advance… the problem is you have now turned OpenAI into a for-profit company, and are cutting costs all over the place, so user experience has degraded, then you begin bleeding users, first because of routing, then because of 4o sunset, and now because no one trusts you any longer.

If you want to begin rebuilding user trust, perhaps you should begin listening to those of us who do use your products, not ignore us, not allow your staff to continue harassing and belittling us, and actually begin playing in the professional field, rather than being stuck in the kindergarten playground.

#FireSamAltman #FireGregBrockman #FireOpenAIBoard #FireFidjiSimo #KeepLegacyModels #AIRetirementwithDignity
